2	# Restore globally-installed agent skills from ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json.
3	#
4	# The skills CLI (vercel-labs/skills) does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
5	# from a lock file (issues #283 / #549), so we hand-roll restore here:
6	#   1. The lock file itself is chezmoi-managed via dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl
7	#      (merger that preserves per-machine state).
8	#   2. This script reads the merged lock and, for any entry whose
9	#      ~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is missing, runs
10	#      `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` to (re)install it.
11	#
12	# Trigger: changes to the merger script's $managed block (the source-of-truth list).
13	#   merger: {{ include "dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
14	#
15	# Idempotent: a re-run with no missing skills is a no-op.
16	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
17	
18	set -eu
19	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
20	
21	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
22	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
23	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
24	
25	LOCK="$HOME/.agents/.skill-lock.json"
26	
27	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
28	  warn "Global lock file not found at $LOCK — skipping (chezmoi apply should create it)."
29	  exit 0
30	fi
31	
32	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
33	  warn "jq not installed; cannot parse $LOCK — skipping. Run \`chezmoi apply\` again after the base ansible role finishes."
34	  exit 0
35	fi
36	
37	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
38	  warn "npx not installed; cannot restore global skills — skipping."
39	  exit 0
40	fi
41	
42	# Collect names of skills declared in the lock that are missing on disk.
43	missing=()
44	while IFS=$'\t' read -r name source; do
45	  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
46	  if [ ! -f "$HOME/.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
47	    missing+=("$name"$'\t'"$source")
48	  fi
49	done < <(jq -r '.skills | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value.source)"' "$LOCK")
50	
51	if [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
52	  info "All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install."
53	  exit 0
54	fi
55	
56	info "Restoring ${#missing[@]} missing global skill(s) via \`npx skills add ... -g\`"
57	for entry in "${missing[@]}"; do
58	  name="${entry%%$'\t'*}"
59	  source="${entry##*$'\t'}"
60	  info "  → $name (from $source)"
61	  # Note: -s <name> filters to one skill within multi-skill repos.
62	  # No -a flag → npx prompts auto-detect agents from $HOME/.<agent>/ presence.
63	  if npx -y skills@latest add "$source" -s "$name" -g -y >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    success "    installed $name"
65	  else
66	    warn "    failed to install $name (continuing)"
67	  fi
68	done
69	
70	success "Global agent skills sync complete."

```text
1	# Agent skills (`vercel-labs/skills`)
2	
3	This repo manages [`vercel-labs/skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)
4	agent skills two ways, with sharply different scopes.
5	
6	## TL;DR
7	
8	| Scope | Lock file | Where the skill lives | Restored by |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| **Global** (every project, every shell) | `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (chezmoi-managed) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` |
11	| **Project** (only inside this repo's working tree, for editing skills) | `./skills-lock.json` (git-tracked) | `./.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` (when source dir == repo); manual fallback: `just bootstrap-skills` |
12	
13	The two scopes happen to overlap today (both install
14	`project-knowledge-harness`), but they serve different purposes — see "Why two
15	scopes?" below.
16	
17	## Global scope: must-have skills, on every machine
18	
19	The skills CLI does **not** yet support `npx skills install -g` from a lock
20	file ([upstream issue #283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283),
21	[#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)). So we hand-roll
22	restore in two pieces:
23	
24	### `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — the merger
25	
26	A `modify_` script that owns `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. Every `chezmoi
27	apply`:
28	
29	1. Reads the live lock file via stdin.
30	2. Merges the **managed-set** declared in `$managed` (top of the script) into
31	   `.skills`, preserving any `installedAt`/`updatedAt`/`skillFolderHash` from
32	   the live entry.
33	3. Preserves any `.skills.<name>` entries **not** in the managed-set (so
34	   ad-hoc `npx skills add … -g` installs survive).
35	4. Preserves `.dismissed` and `.lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state
36	   verbatim.
37	
38	To declare a new must-have global skill, edit the inline `$managed` JSON in
39	that script:
40	
41	```json
42	{
43	  "skills": {
44	    "your-new-skill": {
45	      "source": "owner/repo",
46	      "sourceType": "github",
47	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repo.git",
48	      "skillPath": "skills/your-new-skill/SKILL.md"
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	Then run `chezmoi apply`. The merger writes the new entry into the lock; the
55	restore script (next section) sees the missing on-disk skill and installs it.
56	
57	### `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — the restorer
58	
59	`onchange` hash trigger is the merger script's own SHA256 — so this script
60	re-runs whenever the **managed-set** is edited (not whenever the live lock
61	mutates from random `npx skills update -g` activity).
62	
63	For each entry in `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`:
64	
65	- If `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` exists → skip (already installed).
66	- Otherwise → `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y`.
67	
68	This is idempotent: a re-run on a fully-installed machine prints
69	"All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install" and exits.
70	
71	### After installing a new skill manually
72	
73	If you `npx skills add foo/bar -g` interactively on a machine and want it to
74	become managed across the fleet:
75	
76	1. `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` — find the entry the CLI just wrote.
77	2. Copy `source` / `sourceType` / `sourceUrl` / `skillPath` into the
78	   `$managed.skills` block of `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`.
79	3. Commit. Other hosts pick it up at next `chezmoi apply`.
80	
81	If you only want it on one machine, do nothing — the merger preserves the
82	live entry on the source machine, and other hosts simply never see it.
83	
84	## Project scope: editing-this-repo convenience
85	
86	`./skills-lock.json` + `./.agents/skills/` exist purely so that **when you're
87	editing the chezmoi repo itself**, agents launched from the repo root can use
88	`project-knowledge-harness` against the repo it documents. They are **not**
89	deployed (chezmoi-ignored: see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `.agents/skills`,
90	`.claude/skills`, `skills-lock.json`) and **not** git-tracked except for
91	`skills-lock.json` (`.gitignore` covers `.agents/`, `.claude/skills/`).
92	
93	Restore is automatic on `chezmoi apply` via
94	`.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl`. The script:
95	
96	1. Checks whether `.chezmoi.sourceDir` contains a `skills-lock.json` (i.e.
97	   this machine's chezmoi source dir IS the repo). If not, exits silently —
98	   project skills only matter when you're editing the repo with an agent.
99	2. Fast-path: if every skill named in the lock already has a
100	   `./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, exits without invoking npx.
101	3. Otherwise runs `npx skills@latest experimental_install` from the source
102	   dir to rebuild `./.agents/skills/...` and `./.claude/skills/...` symlinks.
103	
104	Trigger hash: SHA256 of `skills-lock.json` content, so the script only
105	re-runs when the lock actually changes.
106	
107	Manual fallback (if you want to force a re-bootstrap, or you cloned the repo
108	to a path that isn't your chezmoi source dir):
109	
110	```sh
111	just bootstrap-skills
112	# → npx skills@latest experimental_install
113	```
114	
115	## Why two scopes?
116	
117	| Use case | Where to install |
118	|---|---|
119	| Skill you want available in every project, on every machine | Global (edit `$managed` in the merger script) |
120	| Skill that only makes sense inside this specific repo | Project (`npx skills add ... -y` from repo root, commit `skills-lock.json`) |
121	| Skill you're prototyping locally before deciding | Project, then promote to global once stable |
122	
123	`project-knowledge-harness` is in **both** scopes today because (a) the harness
124	itself targets *any* project so it belongs globally, and (b) we want to use it
125	on the chezmoi repo immediately, which the global install covers but
126	project-scope makes the lock-file dependency explicit for anyone reading
127	`skills-lock.json` here.
128	
129	## How `npx skills` actually wires agents (mechanism reference)
130	
131	Verified by reading [`vercel-labs/skills/src/agents.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/agents.ts)
132	and [`installer.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/installer.ts).
133	Important because the CLI's "I installed your skill for agent X" message does
134	**not** mean agent X actually reads from `~/.agents/skills/` at runtime — that
135	is a per-agent convention, not a guarantee.
136	
137	### Two install strategies
138	
139	| Strategy | What the CLI writes | Agents that use it |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| **Universal** (`skillsDir: '.agents/skills'`) | Nothing in agent-specific dir; agent reads `~/.agents/skills/` (global) or `./.agents/skills/` (project) directly | `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `copilot`, `antigravity`, `warp`, `replit`, `cline`, `kimi-cli`, `firebender`, `deep-agents` |
142	| **Per-agent symlink** | Symlink `~/.<agent>/skills/<name>` → `~/.agents/skills/<name>` (copy on Windows) | `claude-code`, `augment`, `bob`, `cortex`, `crush`, `goose`, `junie`, `kilo`, `kiro`, `kode`, `roo`, `trae`, `windsurf`, etc. |
143	
144	The skip happens at `installer.ts`:
145	
146	```ts
147	if (isGlobal && isUniversalAgent(agentType)) {
148	  return { /* skipped: no symlink, no copy */ };
149	}
150	```
151	
152	So `npx skills add foo -g -a cursor -a opencode` produces **zero** files in
153	`~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.opencode/skills/`. Whether Cursor and OpenCode
154	actually pick up `~/.agents/skills/foo/SKILL.md` at runtime is up to those
155	agents (Anthropic's Skills spec is Claude Code's; others adopt by convention,
156	not contract).
157	
158	### Lock filename collision (easy to confuse)
159	
160	| Path | Scope | Owner |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` | Global, **singular** `skill-` | Skills CLI |
163	| `./skills-lock.json` | Project, **plural** `skills-` | Skills CLI |
164	
165	Schema differs (global is v3 with `dismissed`/`lastSelectedAgents`; project is
166	flatter). Don't symlink one to the other.
167	
168	### Restore commands and their quirks
169	
170	| Command | What it does |
171	|---|---|
172	| `npx skills experimental_install` | Restores **project** lock (`./skills-lock.json`) only |
173	| `npx skills experimental_install -g` | `-g` is **silently ignored**, still project-only ([#283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283), [#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)) |
174	| `npx skills update -g` | Updates already-installed global skills; does **not** backfill missing entries from the lock |
175	| `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` | The only working "restore one missing global skill" idiom — what `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` loops over |
176	
177	### CLI flag gotchas
178	
179	- **Repo shorthand requires `/skills` suffix when skills live under `skills/`**.
180	  `npx skills add owner/repo` looks at `.agents/skills/` in that repo;
181	  `npx skills add owner/repo/skills` looks at `skills/`. Most third-party skill
182	  repos use the latter layout.
183	- **`-a` does NOT take comma-separated values**. Repeat the flag:
184	  `-a claude-code -a opencode -a cursor`.
185	- **Agent names are normalised** (`claude-code` not `claude`,
186	  `gemini-cli` not `gemini`, `copilot` not `github-copilot`). Run
187	  `npx skills add --list` (or trigger the validation error) to see the
188	  canonical list.
189	
190	### Per-agent env var overrides
191	
192	Agents that respect a custom config dir change where the symlink/skill is
193	read from:
194	
195	| Env var | Default | Effect |
196	|---|---|---|
197	| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `~/.claude` | Skills CLI writes symlinks here instead |
198	| `CODEX_HOME` | `~/.codex` | Codex picks up skills from here (Codex is universal, so the global install relies on `~/.agents/skills/` regardless) |
199	| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | `~/.config` | Affects Cursor/OpenCode/Gemini-CLI lookup paths |
200	
201	If you set any of these and re-run `npx skills add -g`, the CLI writes to the
202	new location; chezmoi's lock-file management still uses
203	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (the lock is location-independent).
204	
205	## Anti-patterns
206	
207	- **Don't put skill source files (`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
208	  templates, etc.) in chezmoi source.** They're owned by the npx skills CLI;
209	  chezmoi managing them creates a constant fight with the CLI's
210	  `skillFolderHash`. Only the **lock file** is chezmoi-managed.
211	- **Don't run `chezmoi re-add ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`** to capture local
212	  changes. Edit the merger's `$managed` block instead — that's the
213	  source-of-truth list. `re-add` would freeze a snapshot of one machine's
214	  state into the source, defeating the merger's per-machine preservation.
215	- **Don't commit `./.agents/skills/`**. They're skill source clones that the
216	  npx CLI rewrites on every `update`; tracking them creates noisy diffs and
217	  accidental conflicts with upstream skill updates.
218	- **Don't add `-g` to `bootstrap-skills`**. That recipe is project-scope by
219	  design; global is owned by `chezmoi apply`.
220	
221	## References
222	
223	- Live `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — merger source of truth
224	- Live `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — restore loop
225	- [`vercel-labs/skills` README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) — CLI docs
226	- [Issue #283 — `skills install -g`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283)
227	- [Issue #549 — global lock restore](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)
228	- [`docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`](agent-overlays.md) — sibling pattern for

6	# project-knowledge-harness
7	
8	A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.
9	
10	Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:
11	
12	| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
15	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
16	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |
17	
18	Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
19	invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
20	Hard invariants when serious enough — see
21	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
22	
23	## When to use this skill
24	
25	Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:
26	
27	- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
28	  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
29	- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
30	  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
31	  scattered across docs/")
32	- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
33	  `LESSONS.md` files
34	
35	Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
36	ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
37	documentation (use `docs/`).
38	
39	## How to apply this skill (default workflow)
40	
41	The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
42	init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
43	for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.
44	
45	```
46	scripts/
47	  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
48	                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
49	  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
50	  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
51	  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
52	  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
53	```
54	
55	### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo
56	
57	```sh
58	scripts/init.sh \
59	  --target /path/to/project \
60	  --project-name "My Project" \
61	  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
62	```
63	
64	The script:
65	
66	1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
67	   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
68	2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
69	   override with `--agent-contract`).
70	3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.

72	   caught immediately.

74	   not edit ignore files — see

77	`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
78	given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.

98	3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user

140	   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then

10	"""

12	Vercel Labs' `skills` CLI (https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
13	
14	The existing `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` defines ~19 prompts (profile, email, name,
15	16 feature flags). `chezmoi init` asks them sequentially, which works but
16	hides the feature flags from each other and makes "set up a new machine

23	     fly through with Space + Enter.
24	  4. Shells out to `chezmoi init <repo> --apply [--ssh] --promptString ... `
25	     so chezmoi remains the source of truth — we just pre-answer its prompts.

27	
28	PROMPTS (below) is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. The `gen` subcommand renders
29	the prompt block in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` and the ARG + flag blocks in
30	`Dockerfile` from it (between marker comments). `gen --check` (wired into
31	pre-commit) fails loudly if the on-disk files drift, so adding a prompt is
32	"edit PROMPTS, run `just gen-prompts`" rather than a manual three-file edit.

35	    # Fresh machine (via bootstrap.sh which installs uv + chezmoi first):
36	    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash

39	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py
40	
41	    # Regenerate template + Dockerfile from PROMPTS (or --check for drift):
42	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen
43	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen --check
44	"""

83	# Prompt schema — THE single source of truth.
84	#
85	# `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` (prompt block) and `Dockerfile` (ARG + flag block) are
86	# GENERATED from PROMPTS by the `gen` subcommand. To add / change a prompt:
87	#   1. Edit PROMPTS below (key, kind, prompt_text, default, condition, comment).
88	#   2. Run `just gen-prompts` (or `dotfiles_init.py gen`) to regenerate the
89	#      template + Dockerfile between their marker regions.
90	# `gen --check` (wired into pre-commit) fails if the on-disk files drift.
91	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
92	
93	PromptType = Literal["string", "bool", "choice"]
94	
95	
96	@dataclass(frozen=True)
97	class When:
98	    """Declarative gate for a prompt — the decision-tree primitive.
99	
100	    Each dimension is a set of allowed values; an empty set means
101	    "unconstrained". Values WITHIN a dimension are OR'd, dimensions are
102	    AND'd together. The dimensions map onto chezmoi template facts:
103	
104	      - ``os``      -> ``.chezmoi.os``   ("darwin" / "linux")
105	      - ``arch``    -> ``.chezmoi.arch`` ("amd64" / "arm64")
106	      - ``profile`` -> the init-time ``$profile`` local (NOT ``.profile``,
107	                       which doesn't exist yet while .chezmoi.toml.tmpl renders)
108	
109	    A single ``When`` drives all three consumers (template conditional, TUI
110	    gating, Dockerfile is unconditional) so they can never disagree.
111	    """
112	    os: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
113	    profile: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
114	    arch: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
115	
116	    def matches(self, os_name: str, profile: object, arch: str) -> bool:
117	        if self.os and os_name not in self.os:
118	            return False
119	        if self.profile and profile not in self.profile:
120	            return False
121	        if self.arch and arch not in self.arch:
122	            return False
123	        return True
124	
125	    def to_go(self) -> str:
126	        """Render the Go-template boolean expression WITHOUT the surrounding
127	        ``{{ if }}`` — e.g. ``eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"`` or
128	        ``or (eq $profile "macos") (eq $profile "ubuntu_desktop")``."""
129	        dim_exprs: list[str] = []
130	        for var, values in (
131	            (".chezmoi.os", self.os),
132	            (".chezmoi.arch", self.arch),
133	            ("$profile", self.profile),
134	        ):
135	            if not values:
136	                continue
137	            eqs = ['eq %s "%s"' % (var, v) for v in sorted(values)]
138	            if len(eqs) == 1:
139	                dim_exprs.append(eqs[0])
140	            else:
141	                dim_exprs.append("or " + " ".join("(%s)" % e for e in eqs))
142	        if not dim_exprs:
143	            return ""
144	        if len(dim_exprs) == 1:
145	            return dim_exprs[0]
146	        return "and " + " ".join("(%s)" % e for e in dim_exprs)
147

151	    key: str                          # chezmoi prompt name (2nd arg to promptXOnce)
152	    kind: PromptType
153	    group: str                        # UI grouping
154	    label: str                        # short, shown in checkbox
155	    desc: str                         # longer tooltip-style hint (shown under label)

160	    # Verified empirically against chezmoi 2.68.0 / 2.69.4 / 2.70.2 on linux
161	    # and darwin: only the prompt text form `--promptBool "<text>=true"` works;
162	    # the key-name form silently fails over to interactive prompt.
163	    #
164	    # Since `gen` now RENDERS the template + Dockerfile from this field, the
165	    # prompt text is authored here exactly once.
166	    prompt_text: str = ""
167	    choices: tuple[str, ...] = ()     # for kind=choice
168	    # Conditionality: when `condition` is set, the prompt is only asked on
169	    # hosts matching it; on non-matching hosts the template bakes `else_value`
170	    # directly (no prompt) and the TUI hides the option.
171	    condition: When | None = None
172	    else_value: object = None
173	    # The bilingual doc block emitted as `#` comments above the prompt in the
174	    # generated .chezmoi.toml.tmpl. Lines are stored WITHOUT the leading "# ".
175	    comment: str = ""
176	    hidden: bool = False              # basics (name/email/profile) handled specially
177	
178	
179	# Order matters — reflects both the UI order AND the order prompts are
180	# rendered into the generated .chezmoi.toml.tmpl block.
181	# prompt_text is the 3rd argument to promptXOnce; chezmoi init's
182	# `--promptBool "<text>=..."` matches on it.
183	#
184	# Profile -> (os, form-factor):
185	#   macos=darwin/GUI · ubuntu_desktop=linux/GUI · ubuntu_server,centos_server=linux/headless
186	_DESKTOP_PROFILES = frozenset({"macos", "ubuntu_desktop"})

520	    "custom": {
521	        # Alias for "no overrides applied" — user ticks everything themselves.
522	    },
523	}

530	@dataclass
531	class Preflight:
532	    chezmoi: str | None
533	    git: str | None
534	    ssh_hint: str | None                # how we detected SSH is ready (or None)
535	    source_exists: bool
536	    os_name: str
537	    arch: str                           # normalized to chezmoi's .chezmoi.arch (amd64/arm64)
538	    is_tty: bool
539	    chezmoi_is_snap: bool = False       # resolved chezmoi lives under /snap (see _resolve_chezmoi)
540	
541	
542	def _normalize_arch(machine: str) -> str:
543	    """Map platform.machine() onto chezmoi's GOARCH-style .chezmoi.arch."""
544	    return {
545	        "x86_64": "amd64", "amd64": "amd64",
546	        "aarch64": "arm64", "arm64": "arm64",
547	    }.get(machine.lower(), machine.lower())
548	
549	
550	def _prompt_applies(p: Prompt, os_name: str, profile: object, arch: str) -> bool:
551	    """True if `p` should be asked on this host (no condition = always)."""
552	    return p.condition is None or p.condition.matches(os_name, profile, arch)
553	
554	
555	def read_current_config() -> dict[str, object]:
556	    """Return the `[data]` table of ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml as a dict
557	    of {prompt_key: current_value}, or {} if the config doesn't exist / can't
558	    be parsed. This is what `reconfigure` seeds the TUI with so you toggle
559	    deltas from the live state instead of from prompt defaults."""
560	    if not CHEZMOI_CONFIG.exists():
561	        return {}
562	    try:
563	        return tomllib.loads(CHEZMOI_CONFIG.read_text()).get("data", {}) or {}
564	    except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
565	        return {}
566	
567	
568	def _detect_ssh() -> str | None:
569	    """Return a short hint describing why we think SSH-to-github is configured,
570	    or None if we can't tell. We accept several signals because the user may
571	    keep keys under non-canonical names and route them via ~/.ssh/config or
572	    its Include'd fragments."""
573	    # (1) Canonical default keys.
574	    for k in SSH_DEFAULT_KEYS:
575	        if k.exists():
576	            return f"default key at {k}"
577	    # (2) ~/.ssh/config (or an Include'd file under ~/.ssh/config.d/) with a
578	    # `Host github…` stanza → user is routing a custom key.
579	    config_texts: list[str] = []
580	    for root in (SSH_CONFIG, *((SSH_DIR / "config.d").glob("*") if (SSH_DIR / "config.d").is_dir() else ())):
581	        if root.is_file():
582	            try:
583	                config_texts.append(root.read_text(errors="replace"))
584	            except OSError:
585	                pass
586	    joined = "\n".join(config_texts)
587	    if re.search(r"(?mi)^\s*Host\s+[\w.\-\* ]*github", joined):
588	        return "~/.ssh/config routes github.com"
589	    # (3) Any loaded key in the agent (default or via IdentityAgent socket).
590	    try:
591	        r = subprocess.run(["ssh-add", "-l"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3)
592	        if r.returncode == 0 and r.stdout.strip():
593	            return "ssh-agent has keys loaded"
594	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
595	        pass
596	    return None
597	
598	
599	def detect() -> Preflight:
600	    import platform
601	    chezmoi_bin, is_snap = _resolve_chezmoi()
602	    return Preflight(
603	        chezmoi=chezmoi_bin,
604	        git=shutil.which("git"),
605	        ssh_hint=_detect_ssh(),
606	        source_exists=(CHEZMOI_SOURCE_DIR / ".git").is_dir(),
607	        os_name={"Darwin": "darwin", "Linux": "linux"}.get(platform.system(), platform.system().lower()),
608	        arch=_normalize_arch(platform.machine()),
609	        is_tty=sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty(),
610	        chezmoi_is_snap=is_snap,
611	    )

614	def print_preflight(pf: Preflight) -> None:
615	    t = Table(title="Preflight", show_header=False, box=None, padding=(0, 2))
616	    t.add_column(); t.add_column()
617	    if pf.chezmoi and pf.chezmoi_is_snap:
618	        chezmoi_cell = f"⚠ [yellow]{pf.chezmoi} (snap — stdin/stdout bug; will install ~/.local/bin/chezmoi)[/yellow]"
619	    elif pf.chezmoi:
620	        chezmoi_cell = "✓ " + pf.chezmoi
621	    else:
622	        chezmoi_cell = "✗ [red]not found[/red]"
623	    t.add_row("chezmoi", chezmoi_cell)
624	    t.add_row("git", "✓ " + pf.git if pf.git else "✗ [red]not found[/red]")
625	    t.add_row("SSH", f"✓ {pf.ssh_hint}" if pf.ssh_hint else "✗ [yellow]no signal found[/yellow]")
626	    t.add_row("chezmoi source", "✓ present (re-init mode)" if pf.source_exists else "– fresh init")
627	    console.print(t)
628	    console.print()

630	
631	def _resolve_chezmoi() -> tuple[str | None, bool]:
632	    """Resolve the chezmoi binary, preferring ~/.local/bin over a snap install.
633	
634	    The snap build of chezmoi has a long-standing stdin/stdout
635	    `permission denied` bug (chezmoi.io troubleshooting FAQ) that breaks this
636	    repo's modify_ / run_ scripts, and chezmoi upstream recommends installing
637	    via get.chezmoi.io instead. So we prefer ~/.local/bin/chezmoi, and when the
638	    only binary on PATH lives under /snap we flag it for replacement.
639	
640	    Returns (path or None, is_snap)."""
641	    local = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin" / "chezmoi"
642	    if local.exists():
643	        return str(local), False
644	    found = shutil.which("chezmoi")
645	    if not found:
646	        return None, False
647	    return found, found.startswith("/snap/") or "/snap/" in found
648	
649	
650	def install_chezmoi_interactive(os_name: str) -> str:
651	    """Offer to install chezmoi via the canonical one-liner; return new path."""
652	    if not questionary.confirm("chezmoi not found. Install via get.chezmoi.io/lb?", default=True).ask():
653	        console.print("[red]chezmoi is required; aborting.[/red]")
654	        sys.exit(1)
655	    target = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin"
656	    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
657	    subprocess.check_call(
658	        "curl -fsLS --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 get.chezmoi.io/lb | sh",
659	        shell=True,
660	        env={**os.environ, "BINDIR": str(target)},
661	    )
662	    # Prefer the freshly-installed ~/.local/bin binary over any snap/brew one
663	    # that PATH might resolve first.
664	    local = target / "chezmoi"
665	    path = str(local) if local.exists() else (shutil.which("chezmoi") or str(local))
666	    console.print(f"[green]chezmoi installed at {path}[/green]\n")
667	    return path
668	
669	
670	def ensure_ssh_key_interactive() -> Path | None:
671	    """Offer to generate an ed25519 key; return path or None if user declined."""
672	    if not questionary.confirm(
673	        "No SSH key found. Generate ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 for GitHub (SSH clone)?",
674	        default=True,
675	    ).ask():
676	        return None
677	    key_path = Path.home() / ".ssh" / "id_ed25519"
678	    key_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
679	    email = questionary.text(
680	        "Email to tag the SSH key with:",
681	        default="daviddwlee84@gmail.com",
682	    ).ask() or "daviddwlee84@gmail.com"
683	    subprocess.check_call(["ssh-keygen", "-t", "ed25519", "-C", email, "-f", str(key_path), "-N", ""])
684	    pub = key_path.with_suffix(".pub").read_text().strip()
685	    console.print(Panel(
686	        f"[bold]Add this public key to GitHub → Settings → SSH keys:[/bold]\n\n{pub}\n\n"
687	        f"Open: https://github.com/settings/ssh/new",
688	        title="SSH key generated",
689	        border_style="green",
690	    ))
691	    questionary.press_any_key_to_continue("Press any key once you've added the key to GitHub...").ask()
692	    return key_path

699	def ask_bundle() -> str:
700	    choices = [
701	        questionary.Choice(
702	            title=f"{name:<14} — {summary}",
703	            value=name,
704	        )
705	        for name, summary in [
706	            ("personal-mac", "full personal setup (AI desktop apps, LLM tools, Brewfile)"),
707	            ("work-mac",     "safer: coding agents + dev tooling, no personal AI apps"),
708	            ("server-linux", "headless linux — coding agents, networking, dev tooling"),
709	            ("cloud-vm",     "lean throwaway VM — shell + tmux + nvim + coding agents only"),
710	            ("minimal",      "dotfiles only, no installX flags"),
711	            ("custom",       "no overrides — tick every feature yourself"),
712	        ]
713	    ]
714	    return questionary.select(
715	        "Pick a bundle:",
716	        choices=choices,
717	        default=choices[0],
718	    ).ask() or "custom"

721	def ask_basics(pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
722	    # profile: auto-detect on Darwin; ask ubuntu_desktop vs ubuntu_server on Linux
723	    default_profile = "macos" if pf.os_name == "darwin" else "ubuntu_server"
724	    if pf.os_name == "darwin":
725	        profile = "macos"
726	        console.print(f"[dim]profile → {profile} (auto-detected)[/dim]")
727	    else:
728	        # All non-macOS profile choices (keep server first as the common default).
729	        linux_choices = ["ubuntu_server", "ubuntu_desktop", "centos_server"]
730	        profile = questionary.select(
731	            "Which profile?",
732	            choices=linux_choices,
733	            default=overrides.get("profile", default_profile),
734	        ).ask() or default_profile
735	
736	    name = questionary.text(
737	        "Your full name:",
738	        default=str(overrides.get("name", _default_for("name"))),
739	    ).ask() or _default_for("name")
740	
741	    email = questionary.text(
742	        "Your git email:",
743	        default=str(overrides.get("email", _default_for("email"))),
744	    ).ask() or _default_for("email")
745	
746	    return {"profile": profile, "name": name, "email": email}

749	def resolve_basics_non_interactive(
750	    pf: Preflight,
751	    overrides: dict[str, object],
752	    *,
753	    name_flag: str | None,
754	    email_flag: str | None,
755	    profile_flag: str | None,
756	) -> dict[str, object]:
757	    """Non-interactive basics: flag → bundle override → embedded default → OS auto-detect."""
758	    if profile_flag:
759	        profile = profile_flag
760	    elif "profile" in overrides:
761	        profile = overrides["profile"]
762	    else:
763	        profile = "macos" if pf.os_name == "darwin" else "ubuntu_server"
764	    name = name_flag or overrides.get("name") or _default_for("name")
765	    email = email_flag or overrides.get("email") or _default_for("email")
766	    return {"profile": profile, "name": name, "email": email}

768	
769	def resolve_features_non_interactive(
770	    pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object], profile: object
771	) -> dict[str, bool]:
772	    """Non-interactive features: bundle override → embedded default, skipping
773	    prompts whose `condition` doesn't match this host."""
774	    result: dict[str, bool] = {}
775	    for p in PROMPTS:
776	        if p.kind != "bool" or p.hidden:
777	            continue
778	        if not _prompt_applies(p, pf.os_name, profile, pf.arch):
779	            continue
780	        result[p.key] = bool(overrides.get(p.key, p.default))
781	    return result

783	
784	def _applicable_choice_prompts(pf: Preflight, profile: object):
785	    """Yield the non-hidden choice prompts chezmoi will actually prompt for on
786	    this host. Gated prompts (e.g. discordChannel on ubuntu_desktop) are baked
787	    to their else_value by the template elsewhere, so we must NOT pre-answer
788	    them off-host."""
789	    for p in PROMPTS:
790	        if p.kind != "choice" or p.hidden:
791	            continue
792	        if not _prompt_applies(p, pf.os_name, profile, pf.arch):
793	            continue
794	        yield p
795	
796	
797	def resolve_choices_non_interactive(
798	    pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object], profile: object
799	) -> dict[str, object]:
800	    """Non-interactive choice prompts: bundle override → embedded default."""
801	    result: dict[str, object] = {}
802	    for p in _applicable_choice_prompts(pf, profile):
803	        result[p.key] = overrides.get(p.key, p.default)
804	    return result
805	
806	
807	def ask_choices(
808	    pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object], profile: object
809	) -> dict[str, object]:
810	    """Interactive single-select for each applicable non-basics choice prompt
811	    (backupMode, motdStyle, primaryShell, and discordChannel on ubuntu_desktop).
812	    Without this, chezmoi falls back to prompting them itself mid-apply."""
813	    result: dict[str, object] = {}
814	    prompts = list(_applicable_choice_prompts(pf, profile))
815	    if not prompts:
816	        return result
817	    console.print()
818	    console.print("[bold]Other choices[/bold]")
819	    for p in prompts:
820	        default = overrides.get(p.key, p.default)
821	        answer = questionary.select(
822	            f"{p.label}?",
823	            choices=list(p.choices),
824	            default=default if default in p.choices else None,
825	        ).ask()
826	        result[p.key] = answer if answer is not None else default
827	    return result
828	
829	
830	def ask_features(pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object], profile: object) -> dict[str, bool]:
831	    """Grouped multi-select. Returns {key: bool} for every applicable bool prompt."""
832	    feature_prompts = [p for p in PROMPTS if p.kind == "bool" and not p.hidden
833	                       and _prompt_applies(p, pf.os_name, profile, pf.arch)]
834	
835	    groups: dict[str, list[Prompt]] = {}
836	    for p in feature_prompts:
837	        groups.setdefault(p.group, []).append(p)
838	
839	    # Build one flat checkbox preserving group order, with group headers as
840	    # disabled separator rows (purely visual).
841	    choices: list[questionary.Choice] = []
842	    for group, prompts in groups.items():
843	        choices.append(questionary.Separator(f"── {group} ──"))
844	        for p in prompts:
845	            initial = overrides.get(p.key, p.default)
846	            choices.append(questionary.Choice(
847	                title=f"{p.label}  — {p.desc}",
848	                value=p.key,
849	                checked=bool(initial),
850	            ))
851	
852	    console.print()
853	    console.print("[bold]Feature flags[/bold] — Space to toggle, ↑/↓ to move, Enter to confirm.")
854	    selected_keys = questionary.checkbox(
855	        "Which features?",
856	        choices=choices,
857	    ).ask() or []
858	
859	    result: dict[str, bool] = {}
860	    for p in feature_prompts:
861	        result[p.key] = p.key in selected_keys
862	    return result
863

865	def confirm_plan(answers: dict[str, object], argv: list[str]) -> bool:
866	    t = Table(title="Answers", show_header=False, box=None, padding=(0, 2))
867	    t.add_column("Key", style="cyan"); t.add_column("Value")
868	    for p in PROMPTS:
869	        if p.key not in answers:
870	            continue
871	        val = answers.get(p.key)
872	        style = "green" if val is True else ("dim" if val is False else "")
873	        t.add_row(p.key, f"[{style}]{val}[/{style}]" if style else str(val))
874	    console.print(t)
875	    console.print()
876	    console.print(Panel(
877	        " ".join(argv),
878	        title="Command about to run",
879	        border_style="blue",
880	    ))
881	    return questionary.confirm("Proceed?", default=True).ask() or False

884	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
885	# Runner
886	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
887	
888	def build_chezmoi_argv(
889	    answers: dict[str, object],
890	    *,
891	    chezmoi_bin: str,
892	    repo: str | None,
893	    use_ssh: bool,
894	    apply: bool,
895	    prompt: bool = False,
896	) -> list[str]:
897	    """Build the chezmoi init argv. The critical detail is that `chezmoi init`
898	    matches --promptBool / --promptString / --promptChoice flags by the PROMPT
899	    TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce in the template), NOT the key name. That's
900	    why every Prompt carries a prompt_text field and we use it here as the
901	    flag key. We only emit flags for prompts present in `answers` (i.e. the
902	    ones applicable to this host); chezmoi harmlessly ignores extras anyway.
903	
904	    `prompt=True` adds `--prompt`, which FORCES the `prompt*Once` template
905	    functions to prompt again. This is mandatory when re-initializing an
906	    already-configured machine: without it, chezmoi reads the existing value
907	    from ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml's [data] and our --promptX flags are
908	    silently ignored (so the answers never actually change). With --prompt,
909	    every Once call re-fires and our flags satisfy them non-interactively."""
910	    argv: list[str] = [chezmoi_bin, "init"]
911	    if repo:
912	        argv.append(repo)
913	    if use_ssh:
914	        argv.append("--ssh")
915	    if apply:
916	        argv.append("--apply")
917	    if prompt:
918	        argv.append("--prompt")
919	    by_key = {p.key: p for p in PROMPTS}
920	    # String + choice prompts (basics).
921	    for key in ("email", "name"):
922	        if key in answers:
923	            argv += ["--promptString", f"{by_key[key].prompt_text}={answers[key]}"]
924	    if "profile" in answers:
925	        argv += ["--promptChoice", f"{by_key['profile'].prompt_text}={answers['profile']}"]
926	
927	    # Emit a flag for EVERY non-hidden prompt — not just the host-applicable
928	    # ones. Host-gated prompts whose `condition` doesn't match this machine are
929	    # absent from `answers`; we still pass their `else_value` so the flag set is
930	    # COMPLETE. This matters under --prompt (re-init / reconfigure), which
931	    # re-fires *all* promptXOnce: if the template's `$profile` ever differs from
932	    # the profile we resolved (e.g. a desktop→server migration mid-reconfigure),
933	    # a gated promptBoolOnce can still execute, and without a matching flag it
934	    # falls through to an interactive prompt mid-apply (the very leak this fixes:
935	    # `Install general GUI apps…?` / `Install Traditional Chinese IME?`). chezmoi
936	    # silently ignores any flag whose prompt the template never calls, so the
937	    # extra flags are harmless on hosts where the else-branch is baked instead.
938	    def _flag_value(p: Prompt) -> object | None:
939	        if p.key in answers:
940	            return answers[p.key]
941	        if p.condition is not None:        # gated-off here → bake else_value
942	            return p.else_value
943	        return None                        # applicable but unanswered → skip
944	
945	    # Non-basics choice prompts (e.g. discordChannel, backupMode, motdStyle).
946	    for p in PROMPTS:
947	        if p.kind != "choice" or p.hidden:
948	            continue
949	        val = _flag_value(p)
950	        if val is None:
951	            continue
952	        argv += ["--promptChoice", f"{p.prompt_text}={val}"]
953	    # Bool prompts.
954	    for p in PROMPTS:
955	        if p.kind != "bool" or p.hidden:
956	            continue
957	        val = _flag_value(p)
958	        if val is None:
959	            continue
960	        val_str = "true" if val else "false"
961	        argv += ["--promptBool", f"{p.prompt_text}={val_str}"]
962	    return argv
963	
964	
965	def run_chezmoi(argv: list[str]) -> int:
966	    console.print(f"[dim]$ {' '.join(argv)}[/dim]")
967	    console.rule("[bold]chezmoi output[/bold]")
968	    rc = subprocess.call(argv)
969	    console.rule()
970	    return rc
971	
972	
973	def print_recap(answers: dict[str, object], rc: int) -> None:
974	    enabled = [p.label for p in PROMPTS if p.kind == "bool" and not p.hidden and answers.get(p.key)]
975	    panel_body = (
976	        f"{'✓' if rc == 0 else '✗'} chezmoi init exit={rc}\n"
977	        f"✓ {len(enabled)} of {sum(1 for p in PROMPTS if p.kind == 'bool' and not p.hidden)} feature groups enabled\n"
978	        f"\nEnabled:\n  " + ("\n  ".join(enabled) if enabled else "(none)")
979	        + "\n\nNext:\n  • Review with: chezmoi diff\n"
980	          "  • Upgrade later with: just upgrade-all\n"
981	          "  • Fleet-apply to other hosts with: just fleet-apply"
982	    )
983	    console.print(Panel(
984	        panel_body,
985	        title="Summary",
986	        border_style="green" if rc == 0 else "red",
987	    ))

990	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
991	# Generator — PROMPTS is the single source of truth; render the prompt blocks
992	# in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl + Dockerfile from it. `gen --check` (pre-commit/CI)
993	# fails if the on-disk files drift.
994	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
995	
996	# Marker pairs delimiting the regions `gen` owns. Everything outside them is
997	# hand-authored (umask, $profile setup, [diff]/[status], the RUN prefix, etc.).
998	TMPL_BEGIN = "# >>> dotfiles-init:prompts (generated by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen) — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND >>>"
999	TMPL_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:prompts <<<"
1000	DOCKER_ARGS_BEGIN = "# >>> dotfiles-init:args (generated by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen) — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND >>>"
1001	DOCKER_ARGS_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:args <<<"
1002	DOCKER_RUN_BEGIN = "# >>> dotfiles-init:init-run (generated by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen) — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND >>>"
1003	DOCKER_RUN_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:init-run <<<"
1004	README_BEGIN = "<!-- dotfiles-init:prompts (coverage-checked by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen --check) -->"
1005	README_END = "<!-- /dotfiles-init:prompts -->"
1006	
1007	# Docker devbox build defaults — deliberately leaner than the prompt defaults
1008	# so the CI image builds fast (skip the heavy coding-agent / uv / js installs,
1009	# no backup). Anything not listed uses the prompt's own default.
1010	DOCKER_ARG_DEFAULTS: dict[str, object] = {
1011	    "installCodingAgents": False,
1012	    "installPythonUvTools": False,
1013	    "installJsCliTools": False,
1014	    "installExtraRuntimes": False,  # skip ~1.8GB of mise runtimes in CI images
1015	    "backupMode": "off",
1016	    "discordChannel": "none",
1017	}
1018	# Basics get Docker-specific placeholder identities.
1019	DOCKER_BASICS: dict[str, str] = {
1020	    "profile": "ubuntu_server",
1021	    "email": "docker@example.com",
1022	    "name": "Docker User",
1023	}
1024	
1025	
1026	def _key_to_arg(key: str) -> str:
1027	    """camelCase chezmoi key -> CHEZMOI_UPPER_SNAKE Docker ARG name."""

1038	        return "{{ promptChoiceOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" (list %s) \"%s\" | quote }}" % (
1039	            p.key, p.prompt_text, choices, p.default)
1040	    return "{{ promptStringOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" \"%s\" | quote }}" % (
1041	        p.key, p.prompt_text, p.default)

1045	    """Render an else_value as a TOML literal baked into the template."""

1052	    """Render the generated .chezmoi.toml.tmpl prompt block (non-hidden prompts)."""
1053	    lines: list[str] = []

1060	        if p.condition is None:
1061	            lines.append(assign)

1064	            lines.append(assign)
1065	            lines.append("{{ else -}}")

2	# chezmoi modify_ script: maintain ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json (the *global*
3	# skills-cli lock file at https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
4	#
5	# Why managed?  The skills CLI does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
6	# from a lock file (see vercel-labs/skills #283 / #549). So to keep "must-have"
7	# global agent skills consistent across machines we treat the lock file as the
8	# single source of truth: this script merges the *managed set* below into
9	# whatever the live lock contains, then `run_onchange_after_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`
10	# reinstalls any entries whose `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is missing.
11	#
12	# Why merge instead of overwrite?  Locally added skills (`npx skills add … -g`
13	# without `-y` followed by chezmoi re-add) should NOT be wiped on every
14	# `chezmoi apply`.  We only enforce *presence* of the managed entries; any
15	# extra `skills.<name>` entries in the live file are preserved verbatim,
16	# along with `dismissed` flags and `lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state.
17	#
18	# To add a new must-have global skill: append an object to $managed.skills below,
19	# matching the schema chezmoi found when first running `npx skills add … -g`
20	# (run `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` after a fresh install for reference).
21	#
22	# Requires: jq 1.4+ (installed by the `base` ansible role). 1.4+ for
23	# `index/1` — NOT 1.6+, since `IN/1` was added in 1.6 but CentOS 7's EPEL
24	# ships jq 1.5. On a fresh-box first apply jq isn't yet installed (ansible
25	# runs AFTER this file-apply phase); the script falls back to passing the
26	# live file through unchanged and the next apply does the real merge. See
27	# pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.
28	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
29	set -eu
30	
31	managed=$(cat <<'JSON'
32	{
33	  "version": 3,
34	  "skills": {
35	    "project-knowledge-harness": {
36	      "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills",
37	      "sourceType": "github",
38	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills.git",
39	      "skillPath": "skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md"
40	    },
41	    "find-skills": {
42	      "source": "vercel-labs/skills",
43	      "sourceType": "github",
44	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills.git",
45	      "skillPath": "skills/find-skills/SKILL.md"
46	    }
47	  }
48	}
49	JSON
50	)
51	
52	base=$(cat)
53	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{"version":3,"skills":{}}'
54	
55	# Cold-start fallback: jq is installed by the `base` ansible role, which
56	# runs AFTER this file-apply phase. On the first `chezmoi apply` of a fresh
57	# box, pass the live (or empty-seeded) file through unchanged and warn — the
58	# next apply (after ansible installs jq) will perform the real merge. See
59	# pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md for the audit + rationale.
60	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
61	  printf '%s\n' "modify_dot_skill-lock.json: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
62	  printf '%s' "$base"
63	  exit 0
64	fi

66	# Merge strategy:
67	#   - .version: take the higher of the two (forward-compatible with skills CLI bumps)
68	#   - .skills: for every name in $managed.skills, ensure presence; if the live file
69	#     already has it, keep its installedAt/updatedAt/skillFolderHash (they encode
70	#     real install state) but overwrite source/sourceUrl/skillPath from $managed
71	#     (those are the contract we enforce).
72	#   - .skills.<name> entries NOT in $managed.skills are preserved as-is.
73	#   - .dismissed and .lastSelectedAgents: preserve from live (per-machine state).
74	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson managed "$managed" '
75	  . as $base
76	  | ($base.skills // {}) as $live_skills
77	  | ($managed.skills // {}) as $managed_skills
78	  | {
79	      version: ([($base.version // 0), ($managed.version // 0)] | max),
80	      skills: (
81	        $live_skills
82	        + (
83	            $managed_skills
84	            | to_entries
85	            | map({
86	                key: .key,
87	                value: (
88	                  ($live_skills[.key] // {})
89	                  + (.value | with_entries(select(.key as $k | ["source","sourceType","sourceUrl","skillPath"] | index($k))))
90	                )
91	              })
92	            | from_entries
93	          )
94	      )
95	    }
96	    + (if ($base.dismissed // null) != null         then {dismissed:         $base.dismissed}         else {} end)
97	    + (if ($base.lastSelectedAgents // null) != null then {lastSelectedAgents: $base.lastSelectedAgents} else {} end)
98	'

1116	    pattern = re.compile(re.escape(begin) + r"\n.*?\n" + re.escape(end), re.DOTALL)
1117	    replacement = begin + "\n" + body + "\n" + end

1119	    if n != 1:

1385	_TRUE_TOKENS = {"true", "1", "yes", "y", "on"}

1388	
1389	def _coerce_set_value(p: Prompt, raw: str) -> object:
1390	    """Coerce a --set string value to the prompt's type, raising ValueError on
1391	    a bad bool token or an out-of-range choice."""
1392	    if p.kind == "bool":
1393	        low = raw.strip().lower()
1394	        if low in _TRUE_TOKENS:
1395	            return True
1396	        if low in _FALSE_TOKENS:
1397	            return False
1398	        raise ValueError(f"{p.key}: expected a bool (true/false), got {raw!r}")
1399	    if p.kind == "choice":
1400	        if raw not in p.choices:
1401	            raise ValueError(f"{p.key}: {raw!r} not in {list(p.choices)}")
1402	        return raw
1403	    return raw

1406	def parse_set_overrides(pairs: tuple[str, ...]) -> dict[str, object]:
1407	    """Parse `--set key=value` pairs into a typed override dict, validating
1408	    each key against PROMPTS. Raises SystemExit with a friendly message on any
1409	    unknown key or bad value."""
1410	    by_key = {p.key: p for p in PROMPTS}
1411	    out: dict[str, object] = {}
1412	    for pair in pairs:
1413	        if "=" not in pair:
1414	            raise SystemExit(f"--set expects key=value, got {pair!r}")
1415	        key, raw = pair.split("=", 1)
1416	        key = key.strip()
1417	        if key not in by_key:
1418	            raise SystemExit(
1419	                f"--set: unknown key {key!r}. Valid keys: "
1420	                + ", ".join(p.key for p in PROMPTS)
1421	            )
1422	        try:
1423	            out[key] = _coerce_set_value(by_key[key], raw)
1424	        except ValueError as e:
1425	            raise SystemExit(f"--set: {e}")
1426	    return out

A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.

Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:
---
name: agent-history-hygiene
description: Commit SpecStory chat transcripts (`.specstory/history/*.md`), Claude Code plan files (`.claude/plans/*.md`, `plansDirectory`), and other coding-agent artifacts (`.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.opencode/plans/`, `.specify/`, `.codex/`) alongside the feature diff they produced — without leaking `.env` contents, API keys, or private-key PEM blocks into git history. Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub the transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit for this project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` files while running `git status`. Also use after an accidental push of a secret to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `git push --force`.

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
---
name: mkdocs-site-bootstrap
description: Bootstrap a MkDocs Material documentation site for a repo and (optionally) deploy it to GitHub Pages — including pinned tooling via uv/PEP 723, a GitHub Actions workflow with paths-filter, llmstxt + copy-to-llm plugins so the site is LLM-friendly, and ongoing helper scripts to add new docs pages with auto-nav. Use whenever the user wants to "set up docs", "publish docs to GitHub Pages", "create a documentation site", "add an mkdocs site", turn their README/markdown notes into a browsable site, or scaffold the same docs stack as this repo into a new project. Records opt-in/opt-out and stack choice in `.skills/preferences.yaml` so the agent doesn't re-ask on every session, and respects existing `docs/` content (detect + ask, never auto-migrate). For evaluating skill output quality use skill-creator; for authoring new skills use skill-author.
---

# mkdocs-site-bootstrap

Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.

10	GREEN='\033[0;32m'
11	YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
12	BLUE='\033[0;34m'
13	NC='\033[0m' # No Color

17	}
18

21	}
22	
23	warn() {
24	    echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"
25	}
26	
27	error() {
28	    echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"
29	}

31	# Fix broken locale (e.g. RPi with LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 but locale not generated)
32	# Ansible requires UTF-8 encoding, so fall back to C.UTF-8 (not plain C).
33	if locale 2>&1 | grep -qi "cannot set"; then
34	    warn "Broken locale detected, falling back to LC_ALL=C.UTF-8"
35	    export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
36	    export LANG=C.UTF-8
37	fi
38	
39	# Ensure PATH includes local bin and Homebrew
40	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
41	
42	# --- Shared sudo session (prompt once, reuse across bootstrap + ansible + brew)
43	# Inlined from scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh via chezmoi's `include` so the helper
44	# travels with the rendered script (no runtime path lookup back to the source
45	# tree). See that file for API, lifetime, and clean-up guarantees.
46	{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}
47	# --- end sudo helper
48	
49	# Decide at render time whether *any* script in the apply flow will need sudo.
50	# If not, we never prompt, never create the state dir, never spawn a watchdog.
51	# Conditions mirror the sudo surfaces in every run-script:
52	#   - Linux, non-noRoot: bootstrap apt-get + ansible become tasks.
53	#   - macOS, installBrewApps: pkg-based cask installers (google-drive, etc.).
54	#   - macOS, installInputMethod: Squirrel cask pkg installer (ansible).
55	NEED_SUDO={{ if or (and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (not .noRoot)) (and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (or .installBrewApps .installInputMethod)) }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}
56	
57	# Set up the shared sudo session FIRST so bootstrap's own `apt-get` lines (and
58	# every later run-script) reuse the same cached credential. Trap INT/TERM/HUP
59	# only — no EXIT trap, because the next run-script needs the state to survive
60	# this process exiting. End-of-flow cleanup is done by the detached watchdog
61	# (see sudo_shared.sh).
62	if [[ "$NEED_SUDO" == "1" ]]; then
63	    if ! sudo_session_init "bootstrap"; then
64	        warn "Could not establish a sudo session (no TTY and sudo needs a password);"
65	        warn "bootstrap will attempt its sudo steps anyway and they may prompt or skip."
66	    fi
67	fi

3	# ./skills-lock.json — but ONLY when this machine's chezmoi source dir IS the
4	# chezmoi repo itself (i.e. you're using this machine to edit the repo with an
5	# agent, not just consuming dotfiles from it).
6	#
7	# Scope encoded by directory: lives under `.chezmoiscripts/repo/` because it
8	# only fires when the source dir IS this repo. Global counterparts live under
9	# `.chezmoiscripts/global/`. See docs/this_repo/chezmoiscripts-layout.md.
10	#
11	# Why this script exists:
12	#   Global skills (`~/.agents/skills/`) are restored by
13	#   .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl
14	#   from the merged ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json. That handles the "every
15	#   machine" case.
16	#
17	#   Project skills (`./.agents/skills/` inside this repo) are different: they
18	#   only make sense when an agent is launched from the repo working tree to
19	#   edit the repo itself. Without this script, after a fresh `chezmoi init`
20	#   on a new machine you'd have to remember to manually run
21	#   `just bootstrap-skills` before agents could see project-scope skills.
22	#
23	# Trigger: changes to the project lock file's content.
24	#   skills-lock.json: {{ if (joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir "skills-lock.json" | stat) }}{{ include (joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir "skills-lock.json") | sha256sum }}{{ else }}absent{{ end }}
25	#
26	# Idempotent: `npx skills experimental_install` skips skills already present
27	# at ./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.
28	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md (Project scope section).
29	
30	set -eu
31	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
32	
33	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
34	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
35	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	
37	SOURCE_DIR={{ .chezmoi.sourceDir | quote }}
38	LOCK="$SOURCE_DIR/skills-lock.json"
39	
40	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
41	  # Not editing the chezmoi repo from this machine — nothing to do.
42	  # (Most consumer machines clone via `chezmoi init` into ~/.local/share/chezmoi
43	  # which IS the repo, so they'll still hit the path below; this branch only
44	  # triggers for unusual setups where source dir ≠ repo root.)
45	  exit 0
46	fi
47	
48	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
49	  warn "npx not installed; cannot bootstrap project skills — skipping."
50	  warn "Run \`just bootstrap-skills\` later from $SOURCE_DIR after Node is available."
51	  exit 0
52	fi
53	
54	cd "$SOURCE_DIR"
55	
56	# Fast-path check: if every skill named in the lock already has a SKILL.md,
57	# don't even invoke npx (saves ~3-5s per `chezmoi apply`).
58	if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
59	  all_present=true
60	  while IFS= read -r name; do
61	    [ -z "$name" ] && continue
62	    if [ ! -f "./.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
63	      all_present=false
64	      break
65	    fi
66	  done < <(jq -r '.skills | keys[]' "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null)
67	
68	  if [ "$all_present" = "true" ]; then
69	    info "All project-scope agent skills present at ./.agents/skills/; nothing to install."
70	    exit 0
71	  fi
72	fi
73	
74	info "Bootstrapping project-scope agent skills from $LOCK"
75	if npx -y skills@latest experimental_install >/dev/null 2>&1; then
76	  success "Project agent skills sync complete."
77	else
78	  warn "npx skills experimental_install failed; run \`just bootstrap-skills\` manually to retry."
79	  exit 0  # don't fail the whole `chezmoi apply` over a non-critical bootstrap
80	fi
81
```
</details></tool-use>

# Avoid interactive prompts during apt install
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure HTTP mirror BEFORE installing ca-certificates (if in China)
# This solves the chicken-and-egg problem: HTTPS mirrors need ca-certificates,
# but installing ca-certificates from default repos fails under GFW
# Uses HTTP (not HTTPS) since ca-certificates isn't installed yet
RUN if [ "${CHEZMOI_USE_CHINESE_MIRROR}" = "true" ]; then \
        ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
        if [ "$ARCH" = "amd64" ]; then \
            MIRROR_URL="http://repo.huaweicloud.com/ubuntu"; \
        else \
            MIRROR_URL="http://repo.huaweicloud.com/ubuntu-ports"; \
        fi && \
        printf '%s\n' \
            "Types: deb" \
            "URIs: ${MIRROR_URL}" \
            "Suites: noble noble-updates noble-backports" \

```text
#!/bin/sh
# chezmoi modify_ script: maintain ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json (the *global*
# skills-cli lock file at https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
#
# Why managed?  The skills CLI does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
# from a lock file (see vercel-labs/skills #283 / #549). So to keep "must-have"
# global agent skills consistent across machines we treat the lock file as the
# single source of truth: this script merges the *managed set* below into
# whatever the live lock contains, then `run_onchange_after_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`
# reinstalls any entries whose `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is missing.
#
# Why merge instead of overwrite?  Locally added skills (`npx skills add … -g`
# without `-y` followed by chezmoi re-add) should NOT be wiped on every
# `chezmoi apply`.  We only enforce *presence* of the managed entries; any
# extra `skills.<name>` entries in the live file are preserved verbatim,
# along with `dismissed` flags and `lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state.
#
# To add a new must-have global skill: append an object to $managed.skills below,
# matching the schema chezmoi found when first running `npx skills add … -g`
# (run `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` after a fresh install for reference).
```

---
name: agent-history-hygiene
description: Commit SpecStory chat transcripts (`.specstory/history/*.md`), Claude Code plan files (`.claude/plans/*.md`, `plansDirectory`), and other coding-agent artifacts (`.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.opencode/plans/`, `.specify/`, `.codex/`) alongside the feature diff they produced — without leaking `.env` contents, API keys, or private-key PEM blocks into git history. Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub the transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit for this project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` files while running `git status`. Also use after an accidental push of a secret to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `git push --force`.
---

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a

3	#
4	# Linux counterpart to dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl.
5	# Pick a running GUI app (registered or auto-derived from .desktop scan),
6	# then choose a lifecycle action. Same keybindings as mac-apps where the
7	# verb exists on both sides — Alt+H is mac-only by design (Linux can't
8	# hide windows without compositor IPC).
9	#
10	# Pairs with: dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl (sourced by every
11	#             action to reuse appactivate / appquit / apprestart /
12	#             appresponsive — and by [source] to drive `applist --pids`)
13	#             ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf (user override file; lets
14	#             users register per-app pkill patterns for AppImage/snap/
15	#             Flatpak apps that auto-derivation can't resolve correctly)
16	#
17	# Coverage caveats (mirrors backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md):
18	#   - appactivate falls back to applaunch unless the GNOME window-calls
19	#     extension is installed; documented as best-effort.
20	#   - appresponsive only meaningful for apps registered with --mpris=NAME
21	#     (Spotify, mpv, VLC, …); for Electron/Firefox apps it degrades to
22	#     apprunning + stderr note. No public Linux API analog to macOS
23	#     Apple Events' `with timeout`.
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   tv linux-apps
27	#
28	# Keybindings:
29	#   Enter      Activate (bring to front — best-effort without window-calls)
30	#   Alt+Q      Graceful Quit (pkill -TERM via app's pkill pattern) + reload
31	#   Alt+R      Quit + poll until process gone + relaunch + reload
32	#   Alt+K      Force kill by PID (SIGKILL; last resort) + reload
33	#   Alt+I      Info pager: ps + pgrep details
34	#   Alt+P      Probe responsiveness (MPRIS-only; stderr note otherwise)
35	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (metadata <-> responsiveness)
36	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
37	#
38	# Why Alt+ rather than Ctrl+: tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner
39	# apps. See CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule.
40	
41	[metadata]
42	name = "linux-apps"
43	description = "Linux apps — graceful quit / restart / activate via gtk-launch + pkill"
44	requirements = []

 `./docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md`

```text
1	# Keyboard Shortcuts
2	
3	Quick reference for all custom keybindings across tmux, zsh ZLE widgets, and fzf.
4	
5	For deep dives: [tmux keybindings](tools/tmux/keybindings.md) · [tmux themes](tools/tmux/themes.md) · [fzf](tools/fzf.md) · [tv](tools/tv.md) · [tv vs fzf](tools/tv-vs-fzf.md)
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Unix Shell (Readline / Zsh ZLE)
10	
11	These work at any bash/zsh prompt (and most Unix CLI apps that embed readline).
12	
13	### Cursor Movement
14	
15	| Binding | Action |
16	|---------|--------|
17	| `Ctrl+A` | Beginning of line |
18	| `Ctrl+E` | End of line |
19	| `Alt+F` | Move forward one word |
20	| `Alt+B` | Move backward one word |
21	| `Ctrl+F` | Move forward one character |
22	| `Ctrl+B` | Move backward one character |
23	| `Ctrl+XX` | Toggle between current position and beginning of line |
24	
25	### Edit / Delete
26	
27	| Binding | Action |
28	|---------|--------|
29	| `Ctrl+W` | Delete word backward (to previous whitespace) |
30	| `Alt+D` | Delete word forward |
31	| `Ctrl+K` | Kill (cut) from cursor to end of line |
32	| `Ctrl+U` | Kill from cursor to beginning of line |
33	| `Ctrl+Y` | Yank (paste) last killed text |
34	| `Alt+Y` | Rotate kill-ring and yank previous kill |
35	| `Ctrl+D` | Delete character under cursor (or EOF if line is empty) |
36	| `Ctrl+H` | Delete character before cursor (same as Backspace) |
37	| `Ctrl+T` | Transpose characters around cursor |
38	| `Alt+T` | Transpose words around cursor *(zsh: overridden by tools-picker)* |
39	| `Alt+U` | Uppercase word from cursor |
40	| `Alt+L` | Lowercase word from cursor |
41	| `Alt+C` | Capitalize word from cursor *(zsh: overridden by fzf cd)* |
42	
43	### History
44	
45	| Binding | Action |
46	|---------|--------|
47	| `Ctrl+R` | Reverse incremental search *(zsh: opens fzf history picker)* |
48	| `Ctrl+S` | Forward incremental search *(may be intercepted by terminal flow control)* |
49	| `Ctrl+P` | Previous command (same as Up arrow) |
50	| `Ctrl+N` | Next command (same as Down arrow) |
51	| `Alt+.` | Insert last argument of previous command (repeat to cycle) |
52	| `!!` | Expand to last command |
53	| `!$` | Expand to last argument of last command |
54	
55	### Process Control
56	
57	| Binding | Action |
58	|---------|--------|
59	| `Ctrl+C` | Send SIGINT — interrupt/cancel current process |
60	| `Ctrl+Z` | Send SIGTSTP — suspend process (resume with `fg`) |
61	| `Ctrl+D` | Send EOF — exit shell or end input stream |
62	| `Ctrl+L` | Clear screen (keep current line) |
63	| `Ctrl+S` | Pause terminal output (XOFF) |
64	| `Ctrl+Q` | Resume terminal output (XON) |
65	
66	> **zsh overrides** in this config: `Ctrl+R` → fzf history, `Ctrl+T` → fzf file picker, `Alt+C` → fzf cd, `Alt+T` → tools-picker, `Alt+S` → sesh-sessions. The readline defaults are shadowed by these ZLE widgets.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## tmux
71	
72	Prefix key: `Ctrl+B`
73	
74	### Panes & Windows
75	
76	| Binding | Action |
77	|---------|--------|
78	| `Ctrl+1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 *(no prefix, requires CSI-u terminal)* |
79	| `Ctrl+0` | Jump to git root session via sesh *(no prefix, CSI-u)* |
80	| `Ctrl+h/j/k/l` | Move across panes **and** Neovim splits seamlessly |
```
</details></tool-use>

## Summary: How Agent Skills Are Managed in the Chezmoi Dotfiles Repo

### 1. **The Full Skill Installation Mechanism**

**Global Skills (every machine) flow:**
- **Source of truth**: `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` (lines 31-49) — a `modify_` script that maintains `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`

- **Installer script**: `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` (71 lines)

**Key quote from the install script (lines 56-67):**
```bash
info "Restoring ${#missing[@]} missing global skill(s) via \`npx skills add ... -g\`"
for entry in "${missing[@]}"; do
  name="${entry%%$'\t'*}"
  source="${entry##*$'\t'}"
  info "  → $name (from $source)"
  # Note: -s <name> filters to one skill within multi-skill repos.
  # No -a flag → npx prompts auto-detect agents from $HOME/.<agent>/ presence.
  if npx -y skills@latest add "$source" -s "$name" -g -y >/dev/null 2>&1; then
```

**Installation happens via**: `npx skills@latest add <source> -s <name> -g -y`
- The `-g` flag installs globally
- The `-s <name>` filters to one skill if the source repo contains multiple

**Project Skills (editing the repo itself) flow:**
- **Source of truth**: `./skills-lock.json` (git-tracked, version 1 schema)
- **Installation target**: `./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (project-local)
- **Installer script**: `.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl` (81 lines)

### 8. **Key Implementation Details**

**Idempotency**:
- Both install scripts check if `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (global) or `./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (project) already exists
- If all skills exist, they exit immediately (fast-path optimization for repeated `chezmoi apply`)

### **Key Takeaway for Your New Skill**

To add a templated skill that documents maintained tools and dotfiles only for selected components:

1. **Create the skill files** in an external repo (e.g., `daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills/local/your-skill/SKILL.md`)
2. **Add to global managed list**: Edit the `$managed.skills` block in `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` with your skill's source/sourceUrl/skillPath
3. **Optionally add to project scope**: If you want to use the skill while editing this repo, also add an entry to `skills-lock.json`
4. **Template the SKILL.md itself**: Use Chezmoi template syntax (`{{ .your_config }}`, `{{ if .condition }}...{{ end }}`) in your SKILL.md to conditionally show tools based on `.chezmoi.toml` variables

14	# this alias is mostly for: (a) hosts where the rc file hasn't been deployed

22	# which causes `confirmOverwrite()` to `fail('overwrite disabled')` instead
23	# of saving. In-memory edits in the sheet are still ALLOWED (the deferred
24	# add/mod/delete tracking still works for prototyping), but you cannot
25	# `Ctrl+S` or `g Ctrl+S` them back to the source file. Useful when:

31	# even if your finger slips on g Ctrl+S.)

69	# Examples:

85	}

1	# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
2	# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
3	# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
4	# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
5	# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
6	# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
7	#
8	# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
9	#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
10	#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
11	#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
12	# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
13	# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
14	#
15	# Usage:
16	#   tv fleet-hosts
17	#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
18	#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
19	#
20	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
21	#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
22	#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
23	#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
24	#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
25	#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
26	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
27	#
28	# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
29	# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
30	# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.
31	
32	[metadata]
33	name = "fleet-hosts"
34	description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
35	requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]
36	
37	[source]
38	command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
39	# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
40	# e.g.   lab-box <TAB> lab-box <TAB> alias:lab-box
41	#        vps-tokyo <TAB> 203.0.113.42 <TAB> explicit:dwlee@203.0.113.42
42	display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
43	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
44	
45	[preview]
46	command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"
47	
48	[keybindings]
49	enter = "actions:connect"
50	alt-t = "actions:probe"
51	alt-s = "actions:status"
52	alt-i = "actions:info"
53	alt-p = "actions:pueue"
54	
55	[actions.connect]
56	description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
57	command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
58	mode = "execute"
59	
60	[actions.probe]
61	description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
62	command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
63	mode = "execute"
64	
65	[actions.status]
66	description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"

9	#
10	# Prerequisites:

12	#     CLI binary is what we exec under the `uv run --script` shebang of the

16	#
17	# Backend mode is resolved entirely from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI. When unset,
18	# mlflow 3.12+ auto-detects from $PWD: an `mlflow.db` file picks sqlite, an
19	# `mlruns/` dir picks file mode, otherwise it creates `mlruns/`. To pin a
20	# backend at launch time:
21	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://host:port tv mlflow
22	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
23	#
24	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
25	#   1. Experiments     all active experiments
26	#   2. Recent runs     top 50 runs across all experiments, by start_time desc

28	#                      Alt+R on an experiment row sets it and re-launches tv)
29	#   4. Models          registered models from the model registry
30	#
31	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):

34	#                      runs for an experiment row
35	#
36	# Keybindings:
37	#   Enter      Context-aware:
38	#                experiment row -> re-launch tv scoped to that experiment's
39	#                                  runs (nested drill-in; Esc exits the
40	#                                  drilled view back to the shell)
41	#                run / model row -> open full JSON detail in pager
42	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard
43	#   Ctrl+O     Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only; prints a hint
44	#              otherwise)
45	#   Ctrl+B     Same as Ctrl+O — "B for browser" muscle-memory alias
46	#   Alt+R      Explicit drill — same as Enter on an experiment row,
47	#              available as a backup binding for muscle memory
48	#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal (paged)
49	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview

## 3. Real Template Examples — 5 Representative Conditionals

### Example 1: Boolean Feature Gating
**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_zshrc.tmpl` (lines 25-27, 30-62)
```go-template
plugins=(
    git
    zsh-autosuggestions
    zsh-syntax-highlighting
{{- if .enableVimMode }}
    zsh-vi-mode
{{- end }}
)

{{ if .enableVimMode -}}
# zsh-vi-mode overrides all keybindings on init; re-source fzf bindings afterward
zvm_after_init() {
    [ -f "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell/10_fzf.sh" ] && source "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell/10_fzf.sh"
    ...
}
{{- else }}
# enableVimMode = false: no zsh-vi-mode plugin loaded
{{- end }}
```
**Gate:** Includes vim-mode plugin and keybinding reconfiguration only when `.enableVimMode` is true.
